codeReview.summary: Clean implementation of JSON plan schema and parser. All four feature requirements are met: (1) plan-json-parser.ts created with PlanJsonSchema, PlanStepSchema, BehavioralAssertionSchema, ReviewFindingSchema, OpenQuestionSchema, PlanReviewOutputSchema, and parseJsonPlan(); (2) ProtoStep already had fileReferences/feature fields — worker correctly verified this and skipped the change; (3) plan-output-extractor.ts updated to prefer .plan.json files with markdown fallback; (4) plan_file_path added to PLAN_DRAFT_FIELDS and PLAN_REVIEW_FIELDS. The schema structure matches the ADR-004 spec's code reference closely. Tests are thorough with 40 cases covering valid/invalid inputs, required/optional fields, and all sub-schemas.

issues.description: behavioralContract array has no .min(1) constraint, but the spec's Schema Rules say 'behavioralContract[] (required, min 1)'. The test 'accepts plan with empty behavioralContract' explicitly validates this permissive behavior. For LLM-produced plans this is arguably safer (avoids rejecting otherwise valid plans), but it deviates from the spec. Consider adding .min(1) to match the spec or documenting the intentional deviation.

EstimatedComplexitySchema is duplicated — identical definition exists in src/queue/proto-step.ts:26. One module should be the canonical source and the other should import from it. This risks the two drifting apart if one is updated without the other.

fileReferences is optional in the Zod schema but the spec's Draft Output Schema interface shows it as required (string[], not string[]?) and the Schema Rules explicitly say 'fileReferences (required)'. The code reference in the migration guide's section 9 also shows it as optional, so the spec has an internal inconsistency. The worker followed the code reference. Consider reconciling the spec to avoid confusion for downstream features.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The json-plan-migration.md spec has contradictory guidance on fileReferences — the TypeScript interface and Schema Rules say it's required, but the code reference in section 9 shows z.array(z.string()).optional(). Similarly, behavioralContract is documented as 'required, min 1' in Schema Rules but the code reference has no .min(1). These inconsistencies could lead different workers to implement different constraints.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: json-plan-migration.md line ~174 says 'fileReferences (required)' but line ~502 shows 'fileReferences: z.array(z.string()).optional()'. Line ~180 says 'behavioralContract[] (required, min 1)' but line ~530 has no .min(1).

sharedStateObservations.observation: Two independent EstimatedComplexitySchema definitions exist (plan-json-parser.ts:26 and proto-step.ts:26) with identical enum values. No convention documented about which module owns shared sub-schemas for the plan/queue boundary.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/controller/plan-json-parser.ts exports EstimatedComplexitySchema; src/queue/proto-step.ts also exports EstimatedComplexitySchema with same values ['trivial','low','medium','high','critical'].

summary: Feature passes review. All four deliverables implemented correctly: JSON plan schema with Zod validation, ProtoStep already aligned (no change needed), plan-output-extractor prefers .plan.json, and plan_file_path added to handoff field specs. Three non-blocking issues found: (1) behavioralContract allows empty arrays despite spec saying min 1, (2) duplicated EstimatedComplexitySchema across two modules, (3) fileReferences optional vs spec saying required (spec itself is inconsistent). Tests are comprehensive with 40 cases. No blocking issues.
